decisions.statement: The credential store is handed in as a function.
The store is asked for the account that met the 401.
A store with no credential for the account ends the attempt.
A store with the token that failed ends the attempt.
A store with a token other than the token that failed is a retry.
Two credentials are told apart by access token alone.
A retry hands back a credential and no account.
An ended attempt hands back the body text read from the original.
An ended attempt hands back the status text of the original.
An ended attempt hands back the headers of the original.
An ended attempt hands back status 401.
A caller cannot tell a missing credential from an unchanged token.
Why an attempt ended is written to the error log.
A retry is written to the output log.
The error log names the whole trail of accounts rather than the current account.
Nothing here reaches a network.
A caller replays each account at most once.
The status handed back is 401 even where the original has another status.
A body that cannot be read throws out of the attempt.
The body is read even where the attempt ends in a retry.
An ended attempt has the content-encoding of a body already decoded.
An ended attempt has the content-length of the compressed body.

definition: what a 401 becomes once the credential store is asked for a newer token
